review_scope: Complete assertion-level map of the function-family file-only pointers in doc/reviews/2038-specification-audit/shards/file_only_reference_assertions_current/inventory.json for the listed clauses. Existing calculator oracle, function parser/fault, sampled interpolation, mesh-function, and errata reviews are referenced only where they cover the same selected assertion. No whole-clause certification.

entries.title: Functions aggregate

pointers.assertion_meaning: Public CPU pixel/readback consumers: Type 2 exponential ramps in axial/radial shadings; Type 4 output and geometry through function-based shading; nonlinear Type 2 function after interpolated mesh parameter; Type 4 parser/comment behavior and tracked calculator witness. Assertions check literal colors/regions, bitwise equivalence of a commented/bare program, selected digit interior/background pixels, or explicit 3.141 result.
pointers.limits: The file exercises these function consumers; it is not a corpus for all function types. In particular its radial ShadingType 3 is not a Type 3 function, and its mesh FunctionType 2 is not a Type 0 sampled function. Shading fixtures use a manually generated xref table and explicit stream lengths, but render() does not assert was_recovered=false.

pointers.assertion_meaning: case.rs is the typed corpus model and source citation/tolerance representation, not a test by itself. Its consumer asserts every stored case has a unique/source-cited record, every Table 42 operator and explicit refusal ground is represented, and the no-operator Domain/Range/output-count rules have cases. The separate reference evaluator is checked against case-authored literal expected values.
pointers.limits: Coverage of this test data set is not exhaustive conformance to PLRM3, all arbitrary input/output dimensions, or every function consumer.

entries.verdict: The pointers are meaningful evidence of actual function-bearing consumers and corpus mechanics, but owner status is broader than either file alone.

entries.title: General; Domain and Range clipping

pointers.assertion_meaning: Type 4 function consumers through Type 1 shading: transformed-domain painted/unpainted pixels, literal red/blue values around a discontinuity, and deterministic whole-grid versus partitioned-grid output. The literal color pixels discriminate function and domain results; grid equality alone is a determinism test.
pointers.limits: The domain-shading tests establish selected two-input consumers, not general m-dimensional clipping. Separate supplemental clipping corpus is more direct for Domain/Range.

pointers.assertion_meaning: Literal, source-cited cases distinguish upper/lower Domain clip, in-domain pass-through, clipping only the second input, lower/upper Range clip, and independent component bounds; explicit output-count cases share this corpus file.
pointers.limits: The GPU Type 1 shading harness skips DomainClip cases because it never evaluates points outside its domain; the reference-corpus assertion still evaluates and checks those cases. This is explicit harness scope, not silently counted GPU coverage.

pointers.assertion_meaning: The separate reference evaluator applies the input clamp before instructions and output clamp after them; corpus test compares to literal expectations.
pointers.limits: Reference adapter explicitly supports up to two inputs for the tested Type 1 shading specialization; do not read this pointer as generic all-m production coverage. Prior `calculator_oracle_assertions_current` reviewed this exact specialization and its scope.

entries.verdict: Strong supplemental literal oracle for selected clipping cases, supplemented by public shading tests; no new test gap found in this mapping.

entries.title: Type 0 sampled functions

pointers.assertion_meaning: This is a Type 4 mesh using a Type 2 nonlinear function; at t=.505 it distinguishes evaluating t² after t interpolation (about 65 red) from interpolating corner colors (about 129).
pointers.limits: Despite the inventory's clause-level pointer, this is not a Type 0 sampled-function fixture; it is evidence for a different function-bearing shading route.

pointers.assertion_meaning: Four independent literal sample bytes are read at all four encoded sample positions. A three-of-four-byte paired stream is refused with required/available byte counts instead of invented zero samples, and a public shading page records that it could not make the mark.
pointers.fixture_validity: The test writes exact object offsets/xref, exact sample stream Length, and same dictionary in the full/short pair; it does not explicitly assert was_recovered=false.
pointers.limits: This is a strong sample extent and consumer test, not all Table 39 interpolation, dimensions, bit widths or Order semantics. Those are covered separately by sampled_functions_spec_audit/current unit assertions.

entries.verdict: No additional Type 0 extent test needed. Existing separately reviewed Type 0 suite exposes B10, the valid small-nonzero-domain interpolation failure; the file-only pointer does not cure or conceal that separate current finding.

entries.title: Type 2 exponential interpolation

pointers.assertion_meaning: The public axial test checks red/blue endpoints and midpoint, radial test checks inner/rim/outside and symmetric points, and mesh test checks post-interpolation nonlinear function semantics. These are literal pixel controls, though the axial/radial midpoint bands allow raster tolerance.
pointers.limits: These are Type 2 functions embedded in shading consumers; not all exponent/domain/vector cardinality combinations.

entries.verdict: Meaningful representative consumer assertions. Unit `an_exponential_function_interpolates_between_its_endpoints` additionally checks N=1 and vector outputs at x=0, .5, 1 and clipped out-of-domain inputs; prior function/clipping reviews cover its limits.

entries.title: Type 3 stitching functions

pointers.assertion_meaning: Search of this file found no FunctionType 3 dictionary: ShadingType 3 is radial shading and must not be mistaken for a Type 3 function.
pointers.limits: Inventory pointer is generic function-shading evidence, not Type 3 stitching-function evidence.

pointers.assertion_meaning: Direct `Function::parse` calls: cycles terminate with named depth refusal; an eight-deep acyclic chain evaluates to .25; a 255-subfunction function succeeds with reversed Encode and x=0→1; a 5000-subfunction function refuses with its observed count.
pointers.fixture_validity: The fixtures manually write offsets/xref and legal function objects for positive chains. The two self/mutual reference graphs are hostile recursion guards. The 5000 stop is the project's local resource budget, not a standard maximum k. No explicit was_recovered check.
pointers.limits: The 255 case proves a realistic k beyond small dimensionality assumptions; it does not prove every `/Bounds`, `/Encode`, boundary equality or nested-function shape. Separate `a_nested_stitching_functions_steps_map_to_the_outer_domain` checks nested mapping. B09 signed-zero endpoint is a separate known failure.

entries.verdict: Positive and safety controls are discriminating; state 5000 limit as resource policy, not ISO upper bound. No new gap isolated by these file pointers.

entries.title: Type 4 calculator functions aggregate

pointers.assertion_meaning: Public page pipeline: actual range-valued function outputs create alpha/color; discontinuity pixel centers assert exact red/blue; comments leave pixel bytes unchanged; tracked BBP file paints source-described glyph-like rectangles; direct Function::parse of the same hand-authored arithmetic returns 3.141.
pointers.fixture_validity: Generated PDF helpers give exact xref offsets; stream Length is explicitly set for function program streams. The corpus BBP test uses a minimal document without xref and tests the function parser directly, not whole-PDF robustness.
pointers.limits: Grid division equality is about determinism, not mathematical correctness alone. Source-derived pixel controls and case/ref evaluator are stronger for expected outputs.

pointers.assertion_meaning: The separate evaluator supplies a second implementation for selected PostScript operator expectations authored as literal values/errors with PLRM citations. It does not by itself certify production or all PLRM semantics.
pointers.limits: Exact operator semantics are delegated by §7.10.5.2 to PLRM3. The prior calculator-oracle audit explicitly treats those citations and local choices separately.

entries.verdict: Useful public-pipeline and supplemental evaluator assertions; not exhaustive Type 4 interpreter proof.

entries.title: Operators and operands

pointers.assertion_meaning: Consumer tests distinguish comment tokenization, actual conditional/calculator paint, and a literal BBP result. They do not independently cover every operator's stack/type/numeric rules.
pointers.limits: The file-only owner pointer does not independently prove Table 42. Unit operator assertions and the separately reviewed PLRM3-backed raster corpus carry that narrower evidence.

entries.verdict: Public calculator consumer behavior is asserted with visible outcomes; no additional operator-level test proposed from this pointer map.

entries.title: Type 4 dictionary, inputs, outputs and errors

pointers.assertion_meaning: Valid Type 4 dictionaries state their input Domain and output Range cardinality; visible colors/alpha and the function-grid partition test show representative use. These are valid-output consumers rather than direct runtime-error controls.
pointers.limits: Input-dependent count/type/stack errors and fault reporting are reviewed in `security_file_only_assertions_current`; do not count these shading tests as equivalent error tests.

pointers.assertion_meaning: Already reviewed in the current function-fault shard; representative valid control versus dynamic output-count/non-number/stack-overflow fault consumers, including post-draw Type 1 grid fault.
pointers.limits: Do not duplicate that fault-path review here. Low-bit image conversion may report a fault at an unused palette level by acknowledged policy; GPU fault reporting remains separate residual.

pointers.assertion_meaning: Corpus data distinguishes expected outputs, named operator errors, undefined cases, and refusal grounds; corpus gate checks literal expectations and explicit rule coverage.
pointers.limits: Data model itself is not a runtime assertion; test consumer is the `tests/corpus.rs` gate.

pointers.assertion_meaning: Separate reference stack caps at 100 and reports stack overflow/underflow states used by cases. The 101-entry refusal case is allowable because the standard requires capacity for at least 100 and does not require more.
pointers.limits: Empty-pop zero is an implementation recovery choice, not a source-derived valid program value; prior calculator oracle review traced §7.10.5.2's normative PLRM3 delegation and the unresolved malformed-stack case.

pointers.assertion_meaning: Contains two explicit output-count error cases in addition to clipping cases; both have source-derived input/output counts and are checked against the independent evaluator.
pointers.limits: No new fault-route claims; production post-interpretation integration is in the reviewed separate function_faults shard.

pointers.assertion_meaning: Explicit refusal grounds and program seeds; stack-depth item pushes 101 against local reference limit 100. Also includes nonstandard bounded-execution/static-analysis grounds that are implementation constraints, not ISO-mandated refusals.
pointers.limits: Keep resource and backend lowering refusals separate from §7.10.5.3's mandatory overflow/error semantics.

entries.verdict: The pointer set separates source-derived errors, explicit local stack/resource limits, public consumer faults, and reference oracle policy. No new test gap isolated; known underflow recovery remains separately qualified.
